rules.topic: Analyze the architecture to identify components
rules.rule: Split the requirement into responsibilities (data, UI, server logic, integration, automation, AI, security, operations) and give each one a component before reading the options.
rules.trap: An option that solves one responsibility well and ignores another

rules.rule: Name the identity at every hop (signed-in user, application user / service principal, managed identity, agent identity), then grant the least privilege to that identity.
rules.trap: Fixing the wrong gate; secrets where a managed identity works; authorization written into a prompt

rules.rule: Check installed apps and platform features (SLAs, queues, duplicate detection, business process flows, timeline, dashboards) before designing anything; build only for a documented gap.
rules.trap: Rebuilding an existing feature with flows or plug-ins

rules.rule: Block the save for every channel → Entity-scope business rule or synchronous plug-in. Form only → form business rule or client script. After the fact → asynchronous plug-in or flow. Long-running or external → flow or Azure Function.
signals: regardless of how the record is created
rules.trap: Client script used for enforcement; synchronous calls to external systems

rules.rule: Standard by default. Elastic for very high volume, time to live and partitioned reads without relational features. Virtual for an external system of record shown without copying. Connector when you only need actions against an API.
rules.trap: Virtual table when the data must be stored; elastic table when charts, business rules or N:N relationships are needed

rules.rule: Data policies decide connector combinations (most restrictive wins; environment policies only add restrictions). Managed Environments add sharing limits, checker enforcement, Pipelines targets and Monitor alerts. Roles, business units, teams and sharing decide rows.
rules.trap: A role to solve a policy problem; Organization access or a business-unit move for one record

rules.rule: Exact, auditable, repeatable rules → deterministic (business rule, Power Fx, plug-in, flow). Free text, summaries, classification → AI with boundaries. Combine: AI proposes, a rule or a person decides.
rules.trap: Letting a model set a value that a rule must determine

rules.rule: Page inside a model-driven app → generative page. New visual for one field or grid → PCF. Behaviour on a form → client script. Standalone pro-code app → code app. UI inside an agent chat → MCP app widget. Conversation → interactive agent. External users → Power Pages.
rules.trap: HTML web resource for new UI; a preview generative-page feature where a GA option exists

rules.rule: Makers, built-in channels, knowledge sources and Power Platform governance → Copilot Studio. Developers, own code or models, SDK evaluation, tracing and Azure governance → Foundry.
rules.trap: Choosing by "which is more powerful" instead of by builders and governance

rules.rule: Pick the reuse unit: PCF control (manifest, solution), client script library (namespaced web resource registered per form), generative page (page or section), canvas component library (canvas apps only).
rules.trap: PCF for behaviour, script for visuals, canvas components on model-driven forms

rules.rule: Flows and canvas apps call connector actions → custom connector (OpenAPI 2.0). Several agents and developer tools → MCP server. Copilot Studio under data policies and ALM → MCP connector in front of the server.
rules.trap: One interface forced on every consumer; client credentials in a custom connector (not supported)

rules.rule: Must hold for every change → plug-in step. Reusable named operation with inputs and a result → custom API (action if it changes data, function if read-only). Something others subscribe to → custom API without a plug-in (business event).
rules.trap: A function that changes data; a step registered to implement a custom API (the main operation is stage 30)

rules.topic: Cloud flows and Copilot Studio workflows
rules.rule: Fixed automation with no agent → Power Automate cloud flow. Tool for a standard-harness Copilot Studio agent → agent flow (agent trigger, Respond to the agent, real-time limit). Automation on the GitHub Copilot harness with native AI actions and agent handoffs → workflow (deterministic path, Copilot Credits).
rules.trap: Agent capacity spent on non-agent automation; a prompt for fixed steps

rules.rule: Listener may be down or several consumers → Service Bus queue or topic. Telemetry stream → Event Hubs. Simple HTTP, low volume → webhook. Must block the save → synchronous plug-in. Inbound writes → alternate key + upsert, idempotent.
rules.trap: Transports that promise exactly once; synchronous calls to external systems inside the save

rules.rule: A standalone pro-code web app on Power Platform hosting with connectors. Prerequisites: Enable code apps per environment, Power Apps Premium for users. Limits: no Power Platform Git integration; assets publicly hosted, so no secrets.
rules.trap: Secrets in app configuration; expecting Git integration

rules.rule: Decide platform, entry point, connection (MCP, A2A, connected agent), identity per hop (delegated / on behalf of the user versus application), where deterministic checks run, and ALM.
rules.trap: Authorization in prompts; a shared admin identity; preview connections in production

rules.rule: Match source and latency: Power Platform Monitor alerts (daily, Managed Environment, 5 recipients, 50 rules per tenant); admin export to Application Insights (24-hour SLA); own telemetry (minutes); Azure metric alerts (about a minute) with action groups; per-item notifications in the flow or plug-in.
rules.trap: A daily mechanism for a minutes requirement

rules.rule: Install base solutions first; read the missing-dependency list; remove references top-down after Show dependencies; managed solutions depend on managed components.
rules.trap: Importing unmanaged or removing components to get past an error

rules.rule: Settings that differ per environment → environment variables (Text, Decimal, Yes/No, JSON, Data source, Secret). Secrets → Secret type backed by Azure Key Vault. Values from the deployment settings file; remove current values before export. Connections → connection references.
rules.trap: A secret in a default value; a connection reference for a URL

rules.rule: The unmanaged active layer wins over managed layers. Upgrade deletes removed components, Update does not; Stage for upgrade lets you migrate data before deletion.
rules.trap: Publishing or re-importing to fix an active layer; Update instead of Upgrade

rules.rule: Targets must be Managed Environments. Delegated deployment (service principal or stage owner) always needs approval. Pre-export step: first stage, before export. Pre-deployment step: after approval, just before import.
rules.trap: Notification triggers used as gates; makers given production rights

rules.rule: Tool Installer first in every job. Export → Unpack → commit; Pack → Checker → Import (holding) → Apply Solution Upgrade; deployment settings file for connections and variables.
rules.trap: Checker after import or before pack; export from Dev used as the build
